name: rlsbl
help: Release orchestration and project scaffolding CLI. Automates version bumping, changelog validation, tagging, GitHub Releases, and CI/CD scaffolding across 17 release targets (npm, PyPI, Go, Deno, Zig, Swift, Hex, Docker, Maven, Dart, Flutter, and more). Ships 53 commands organized into 13 top-level commands and 4 command groups (release, changelog, monorepo, dev).

check.name: check
check.help: Run project checks registered via the check framework and report results

flags.name: all
flags.help: Run every registered check regardless of tag or name filters

flags.name: tag
flags.help: Tag DSL expression to select checks (e.g. 'changelog & !quality')

flags.name: name
flags.help: Glob pattern to filter checks by name (e.g. 'hash-*', '*coverage*')

flags.name: list
flags.help: List all registered checks with their tags and exit without running

flags.name: json
flags.help: Output check results as machine-readable JSON instead of human text

flags.name: ignore-warnings
flags.help: Treat warn-severity results as passing so they do not cause nonzero exit

forwarding.reason: framework-internal: absorbs app-defined global flag values

status.name: status
status.help: Display the current project version, branch, last release tag, unreleased commit count, and changelog coverage. Outputs plain text by default or structured JSON with the --json flag.

flags.name: target
flags.help: Target a specific registry (auto-detected if omitted)

flags.name: json
flags.help: Output version, branch, tag, and coverage as machine-readable JSON

flags.name: registry
flags.help: Query the package registry for the latest published version

scaffold.name: scaffold
scaffold.help: Generate or update CI/CD workflows, git hooks, changelog, and license files. Safe to run repeatedly -- three-way merges template changes with your customizations. Existing files with no stored merge base are healed from their last scaffold commit before merging.

flags.name: target
flags.help: Target a specific registry (auto-detected if omitted)

flags.name: publish-mode
flags.help: Publish mode: "ci" to publish via CI pipelines, or "none" to suppress publishing. Required for private repos; public repos default to "ci".

flags.name: auto-commit
flags.help: Auto-commit scaffolded files after writing them to disk

flags.name: skip-shared
flags.help: Skip processing of shared workflow templates across targets

flags.name: auto-tag
flags.help: Add or update the rlsbl GitHub topic tag on this invocation

check-name.name: check-name
check-name.help: Query npm, PyPI, or other registries to check whether one or more package names are available. Accepts multiple names as positional arguments and respects a configurable delay between checks.

flags.name: target
flags.help: Registry to query for name availability (npm, pypi, go, or github); repeatable

flags.name: delay
flags.help: Milliseconds to wait between consecutive registry API queries (default: 200)

flags.name: json
flags.help: Output results as machine-readable JSON: one object for a single name+target, a JSON array for multiple names and/or targets

claim-name.name: claim-name
claim-name.help: Claim a name on a package registry by publishing a minimal placeholder package. Runs check-name first, then publishes if available.

flags.name: target
flags.help: Target package registry to publish the placeholder to (npm or pypi)

grants.name: publish
grants.reason: claiming a name publishes a real package to a public registry, and neither npm nor PyPI lets you take it back

discover.name: discover
discover.help: Search GitHub for repositories tagged with the rlsbl topic and list them. Use --mine to filter results to only your own repositories. Requires the gh CLI to be authenticated.

flags.name: mine
flags.help: Filter results to only show repositories owned by the authenticated GitHub user

watch.name: watch
watch.help: Poll GitHub Actions CI workflow runs for a specific commit SHA and report pass or fail status. Defaults to HEAD if no SHA is provided. Useful after rlsbl release to monitor the publish pipeline.

flags.name: target
flags.help: Registry whose CI workflow to watch (auto-detected if omitted)

flags.name: run-id
flags.help: GitHub Actions workflow run ID to poll directly instead of searching by SHA

args.name: sha
args.help: Git commit SHA whose CI workflows to monitor (defaults to HEAD if omitted)

pre-push-check.name: pre-push-check
pre-push-check.help: Removed. This command no longer performs any check: it always exits 1 with instructions. The pre-push hook now runs `rlsbl check --tag prepush` instead, so a repo whose hook still calls pre-push-check needs `rlsbl scaffold` to regenerate it.

prs.name: prs
prs.help: List all open pull requests for the current repository using the GitHub CLI. Shows PR number, title, author, and branch for a quick overview of pending work.

unreleased.name: unreleased
unreleased.help: List commits between the latest release tag and HEAD, and check whether each has a corresponding changelog entry. Outputs a coverage report in plain text or JSON to help prepare the next release.

flags.name: json
flags.help: Output the unreleased commit list and coverage status as machine-readable JSON

targets.name: targets
targets.help: List all release targets detected in the current project directory, showing which ecosystems (npm, PyPI, Go, etc.) are active based on manifest files found.

deploy.name: deploy
deploy.help: Run the configured deployment pipeline for the project. Supports named deploy targets and dry-run preview of what would be deployed. Branch restrictions are always enforced.

flags.name: target
flags.help: Registry whose deploy pipeline to run (auto-detected if omitted)

args.name: target_name
args.help: Named deploy target from the project's deploy configuration to execute

commit.name: commit
commit.help: Commit one or more files with an Autogenerated trailer, marking the commit as machine-generated so it is automatically exempted from changelog coverage checks.

flags.name: message
flags.help: Commit message for the autogenerated-file commit (added with Autogenerated trailer)

release.name: release
release.help: Release orchestration commands covering the full release lifecycle. Provides 10 subcommands: run, resume, init, retry, edit, undo, deprecate, yank, scrub, reconcile.

run.name: run
run.help: Bump version, validate the JSONL changelog, run tests and lint, commit, tag, push, and create a GitHub Release. Reads the bump type (patch, minor, major, or infra) and target selection from .rlsbl/releases/unreleased.toml, which can be scaffolded with rlsbl release init. Supports dry-run preview, non-interactive mode with --yes, and --allow-dirty to skip the clean working tree check.

flags.name: push-timeout
flags.help: Timeout in seconds for each git push. Overrides the push_timeout config key; 0 (the default) means use push_timeout, else the shipped default.

flags.name: ci-timeout
flags.help: Timeout in seconds for the release CI gate (the wait for CI to conclude on the pushed release candidate). Overrides the ci_timeout config key; 0 (the default) means use ci_timeout, else the shipped default.

flags.name: check-timeout
flags.help: Timeout in seconds for each preflight check subprocess (tests, lint, external checks). Overrides the check_timeout config key; 0 (the default) means use check_timeout, else the shipped default.

flags.name: hook-timeout
flags.help: Timeout in seconds for each release hook. Overrides the hook_timeout config key; 0 (the default) means use hook_timeout, else no timeout.

flags.name: watch
flags.help: After release, automatically watch CI runs to completion (--no-watch to skip)

flags.name: allow-dirty
flags.help: Skip the clean working tree check and allow releasing with uncommitted changes

flags.name: bump
flags.help: Bump type: patch, minor, major, infra, prerelease. Skips the release file.

flags.name: description
flags.help: Short release description summarizing the changes (required with --bump)

flags.name: preid
flags.help: Pre-release identifier: alpha, beta, rc, stable. Only valid with --bump.

resume.name: resume
resume.help: Resume a previously failed release from where it left off. Reads the in-progress state file (.rlsbl/releases/in-progress.json, or .rlsbl-monorepo/releasables/<name>/releases/in-progress.json for releasable releases), validates that the current branch matches the saved state, and re-enters the release flow, skipping already-completed steps.

flags.name: push-timeout
flags.help: Timeout in seconds for each git push. Overrides the push_timeout config key; 0 (the default) means use push_timeout, else the shipped default.

flags.name: ci-timeout
flags.help: Timeout in seconds for the release CI gate (the wait for CI to conclude on the pushed release candidate). Overrides the ci_timeout config key; 0 (the default) means use ci_timeout, else the shipped default.

flags.name: check-timeout
flags.help: Timeout in seconds for each preflight check subprocess (tests, lint, external checks). Overrides the check_timeout config key; 0 (the default) means use check_timeout, else the shipped default.

flags.name: hook-timeout
flags.help: Timeout in seconds for each release hook. Overrides the hook_timeout config key; 0 (the default) means use hook_timeout, else no timeout.

flags.name: watch
flags.help: After release, automatically watch CI runs to completion (--no-watch to skip)

init.name: init
init.help: Scaffold a .rlsbl/releases/unreleased.toml file by auto-detecting project targets. The generated file contains a default bump type (patch), an include list of all detected targets, and per-target configuration sections for Flutter targets.

retry.name: retry
retry.help: Dispatch CI/CD workflows for a completed release via gh workflow run. Reads the dispatch list and ref from .rlsbl/releases/retry.toml, which is auto-scaffolded with sensible defaults if missing. Verifies the GitHub Release exists before dispatching. Each workflow in the dispatch list is triggered against the configured ref (defaults to the release tag).

flags.name: watch
flags.help: After retry, automatically watch CI runs to completion (--no-watch to skip)

edit.name: edit
edit.help: Sync the GitHub Release notes for a given version with the corresponding CHANGELOG.md entry. Defaults to the current version if none is specified. Use --dry-run to preview changes without updating GitHub.

args.name: version
args.help: Version whose GitHub Release notes to sync (defaults to current version)

undo.name: undo
undo.help: Revert a release. Without --version, reverts the latest release (deletes GitHub Release, removes git tag, reverts version bump commit). With --version, reverts a non-latest release if it is provably unpublished (probes registries for evidence, deletes GitHub Release + tag only, un-finalizes changelog).

flags.name: target
flags.help: Target a specific registry for version detection (auto-detected if omitted)

flags.name: version
flags.help: Version to undo (for non-latest releases that are provably unpublished)

deprecate.name: deprecate
deprecate.help: Mark a past release as deprecated. Sets the GitHub Release pre-release flag and prepends a deprecation notice to the release notes. Use --reason to explain why and --use to suggest a replacement version.

flags.name: reason
flags.help: Human-readable explanation of why this version is being deprecated

flags.name: use
flags.help: Suggest this version as a replacement in the deprecation notice

args.name: version
args.help: Semver string of the release to deprecate, with or without v prefix (e.g. 0.9.1)

yank.name: yank
yank.help: Remove a published version from package registries. Probes each configured target's registry to determine publication status, then executes registry-specific removal: npm deprecate, Go retract, or PyPI manual checklist. Also marks the GitHub Release as pre-release with a yank notice.

flags.name: reason
flags.help: Human-readable explanation of why this version is being yanked

flags.name: use
flags.help: Suggest this version as a replacement in the yank notice

args.name: version
args.help: Semver string of the release to yank, with or without v prefix (e.g. 0.9.1)

scrub.name: scrub
scrub.help: Scrub sensitive content from git history and update release metadata to match the rewritten commits. Supports 3 modes: match (--pattern), file (--file), or recipe (--recipe). After rewriting, remaps commit hashes in JSONL changelog files, regenerates CHANGELOG.md, force-pushes, and recreates GitHub Releases on the new tags.

flags.name: replace
flags.help: Match mode: literal text to substitute for each match (mutually exclusive with --mangle)

flags.name: mangle
flags.help: Match mode: replace matched content with random ASCII of same length (mutually exclusive with --replace)

flags.name: reason
flags.help: Reason for scrubbing (required, used in commit message)

flags.name: pattern
flags.help: Match mode: regex pattern to match against file contents (mutually exclusive with --file and --recipe)

flags.name: file
flags.help: File mode: path of the file to rewrite throughout history; it is replaced with its current on-disk content, or removed if absent (mutually exclusive with --pattern and --recipe; requires --from-commit)

flags.name: recipe
flags.help: Recipe mode: path to a scrub recipe TOML file executed via safegit scrub run; per-operation pattern/replace/mangle live inside the recipe (mutually exclusive with --pattern and --file)

flags.name: from-commit
flags.help: SHA of the earliest commit to rewrite (all descendants are also rewritten)

flags.name: entire-history
flags.help: Rewrite every commit in the repository from the initial commit onward (match and recipe modes only; file mode requires --from-commit)

reconcile.name: reconcile
reconcile.help: Reconcile release metadata with a rewritten history: re-push the tags a rewrite moved and recreate the GitHub Releases attached to them. Reads safegit's rewrite journal (.git/safegit/rewrite-maps.jsonl) to determine what moved, so it works after ANY out-of-band rewrite, not just one driven by rlsbl release scrub. Fail-closed: a tag whose divergence from the remote the journal does not explain is a hard error, never a force-push.

flags.name: push-timeout
flags.help: Timeout in seconds for each tag push. Overrides the push_timeout config key; 0 (the default) means use push_timeout, else the shipped default.

changelog.name: changelog
changelog.help: Structured changelog management using JSONL entries with 3 entry types (feature, fix, breaking). Add and generate CHANGELOG.md from per-commit changelog entries stored in unreleased.jsonl for precise, auditable release notes.

add.name: add
add.help: Append a structured changelog entry to the project's unreleased.jsonl file. Each entry includes a human-readable description, an entry type (feature, fix, or breaking), and optional commit hashes linking it to specific changes. The file is auto-committed by default. Use --no-user-facing to mark internal changes that should not appear in the published changelog.

flags.name: commits
flags.help: Comma-separated list of commit hashes to associate with this changelog entry

flags.name: description
flags.help: Human-readable description of the change, shown in the generated CHANGELOG.md

flags.name: type
flags.help: Classification of the change: feature, fix, or breaking (required if user-facing)

flags.name: user-facing
flags.help: Mark this entry as user-facing (included in generated CHANGELOG.md output)

flags.name: auto-commit
flags.help: Auto-commit unreleased.jsonl after appending the entry

flags.name: allow-batch
flags.help: Auto-create an exclusion if this entry exceeds the commit batch limit

generate.name: generate
generate.help: Compile all validated JSONL changelog entries into a formatted CHANGELOG.md file. Groups entries by type (features, fixes, breaking changes) under the appropriate version heading, preserving existing changelog content for previous releases. Use --dry-run to preview the generated Markdown output without writing to disk, which is useful for reviewing before committing.

flags.name: auto-commit
flags.help: Auto-commit generated CHANGELOG.md and per-version .md files

amend.name: amend
amend.help: Append a changelog entry to a released version's JSONL file. Temporarily unlocks the read-only file, appends the entry, re-locks it, regenerates CHANGELOG.md, and syncs GitHub Release notes. Use --no-validate-hashes to skip hash validation for old or amended commits.

flags.name: version
flags.help: Semver of the already-released version whose JSONL to amend (e.g. 0.39.0)

flags.name: commits
flags.help: Comma-separated commit hashes to associate with the amended changelog entry

flags.name: id
flags.help: Entry ID (ULID) to select the target entry for amendment

flags.name: description
flags.help: Human-readable description for the amended entry in CHANGELOG.md

flags.name: type
flags.help: Classification for the amended entry: feature, fix, or breaking (required if user-facing)

flags.name: user-facing
flags.help: Mark the amended entry as user-facing (included in CHANGELOG.md output)

flags.name: validate-hashes
flags.help: Validate commit hashes via git rev-parse before appending

edit.name: edit
edit.help: Modify an existing changelog entry in unreleased or released JSONL files. Finds the entry by commit hash or entry ID, applies field changes (type, description, user-facing status), and rewrites the file atomically. For released files, temporarily unlocks the read-only file, regenerates CHANGELOG.md, and syncs GitHub Release notes.

flags.name: commits
flags.help: Comma-separated commit hashes identifying the target entry

flags.name: id
flags.help: Entry ID (ULID) identifying the target entry to edit in the JSONL file

flags.name: type
flags.help: New type value (feature, fix, breaking); also disambiguates multi-entry commits

flags.name: description
flags.help: Replacement description text for the matched changelog entry

flags.name: user-facing
flags.help: Set user_facing status on the matched entry (--user-facing to set true, --no-user-facing to set false)

flags.name: auto-commit
flags.help: Automatically commit the edited JSONL changelog file to git after modification

remap.name: remap
remap.help: Remap stale commit hashes in JSONL changelog files using a mapping of old SHAs to new SHAs. Reads the mapping from a file (--map-file), the safegit rewrite journal (--from-journal), or stdin (--stdin). At least one source is required. Auto-commits with Autogenerated trailer.

flags.name: map-file
flags.help: Path to a file of 'old_sha new_sha' lines (same format as git's post-rewrite hook)

flags.name: from-journal
flags.help: Read the commit map from safegit's rewrite journal (.git/safegit/rewrite-maps.jsonl)

flags.name: stdin
flags.help: Read the old/new SHA map from stdin (for piping from git's post-rewrite hook)

monorepo.name: monorepo
monorepo.help: Manage monorepo workspaces with multiple independently-versioned projects. Initialize workspaces, add or remove projects, sync CI workflows, check name availability, and analyze dependency graphs. Supports all 18 release targets in a single workspace.toml. Provides 19 monorepo subcommands: init, add, remove, list, sync, status, check-names, outdated, snapshot, snapshot-check, mirror, graph, impact, extract, absorb, extract-releasable, cleanup, migrate-releasable, rename-releasable. Plus 1 subgroup: release.

init.name: init
init.help: Create a new monorepo workspace by generating the .rlsbl-monorepo directory and an empty workspace.toml configuration file at the current directory. This must be run at the repository root before adding individual projects with the add subcommand. Each workspace tracks multiple independently-versioned projects that share a single git repository.

flags.name: auto-commit
flags.help: Automatically commit the generated workspace.toml configuration file to git

add.name: add
add.help: Register a project directory in the monorepo workspace.toml configuration. The path argument specifies the project's location relative to the repo root. Supports 6 optional settings: display name, target registry, glob patterns for change detection, subtree remote URL, inter-project dependencies, and a library flag to mark shared code packages.

flags.name: name
flags.help: Display name for the project in workspace.toml (defaults to directory name)

flags.name: target
flags.help: Registry this project publishes to (e.g. npm, pypi, go)

flags.name: watch
flags.help: Comma-separated glob patterns for change detection in CI workflows

flags.name: subtree-remote
flags.help: Git remote URL for split-publishing this project as a standalone repo

flags.name: depends-on
flags.help: Comma-separated names of workspace projects this project depends on

flags.name: library
flags.help: Mark as a shared library consumed by other workspace projects (true/false)

flags.name: dev-only
flags.help: Mark as a dev-only leaf node excluded from the dependency boundary guardrail (true/false)

flags.name: releasable
flags.help: Releasable group this project belongs to (name of a [[releasables]] entry, or 'false' to opt out of versioning)

flags.name: registry-name
flags.help: Package registry identity for this project (used verbatim for name checks; overrides prefix/suffix)

flags.name: auto-commit
flags.help: Auto-commit workspace.toml and trigger scaffold/sync commits

args.name: path
args.help: Relative path from the repo root to the project directory to register

remove.name: remove
remove.help: Unregister a project from the monorepo workspace.toml by its path. This removes the project entry from the workspace configuration file but does not delete any files, directories, or git history on disk. The project's code remains intact and can be re-added later with the add subcommand if needed.

args.name: path
args.help: Relative path from the repo root of the project to unregister from workspace.toml

list.name: list
list.help: Display all projects registered in the monorepo workspace.toml file. For each project, shows the project name, relative path from the repo root, target registry for publishing, and any configured options such as watch patterns, subtree remotes, inter-project dependencies, and whether the project is marked as a library.

sync.name: sync
sync.help: Inline every project's CI jobs into a single generated ci-router.yml (and publish jobs into publish.yml) in the shared .github/workflows directory at the repository root. Jobs are inlined rather than routed via reusable-workflow calls because GitHub rejects workflows that reference 20 or more reusable workflows. Stale per-project workflow copies at the root are removed via saferm.

flags.name: auto-commit
flags.help: Auto-commit merged workflow files in .github/workflows/

status.name: status
status.help: Show the current version, last release tag, and number of unreleased commits for every project in the monorepo workspace. Provides a quick overview of which projects have pending changes and are ready for their next release. Projects with zero unreleased commits are shown as up-to-date.

check-names.name: check-names
check-names.help: Check package name availability on a target registry for all projects in the monorepo workspace. Queries the registry API for each project name and reports whether it is available or already taken. Supports optional prefix and suffix arguments to test naming conventions like scoped packages, with a configurable delay between registry queries to avoid rate limiting.

flags.name: target
flags.help: Registry to query for name availability across all workspace projects (npm, pypi, go, or github)

flags.name: prefix
flags.help: String to prepend to each project name before checking availability

flags.name: suffix
flags.help: String to append to each project name before checking availability

flags.name: delay
flags.help: Milliseconds to wait between consecutive registry API queries (default: 200)

outdated.name: outdated
outdated.help: Scan all projects in the monorepo workspace for intra-workspace dependencies that reference older versions than what is currently available in the workspace. Lists each outdated dependency with the referenced version and the latest available version, helping identify which downstream projects need a version bump after upstream releases.

snapshot.name: snapshot
snapshot.help: Regenerate the committed JSON artifact at .rlsbl-monorepo/snapshot.json summarizing all packages, versions, dependencies, and graph structure, and commit it. Verifying without regenerating is a separate command, `rlsbl monorepo snapshot-check`. Under --dry-run the artifact is computed but neither written nor committed, and the preview names both steps.

snapshot-check.name: snapshot-check
snapshot-check.help: Verify that .rlsbl-monorepo/snapshot.json matches the workspace it describes, without regenerating it. Exits 1 when the artifact is stale or missing. This is the read-only half of the former `monorepo snapshot --check` flag; `rlsbl monorepo snapshot` is the half that writes.

mirror.name: mirror
mirror.help: Reconcile a monorepo project's subtree mirror toward its desired state. The mirror is a tool-owned, derived artifact: it observes the remote, then converges it to exactly one scaffold commit atop the current deterministic subtree split, force-pushing (with lease) as the routine write. A tripwire refuses to touch a mirror carrying foreign (hand-authored) commits. Use --dry-run to print a plan (converged, behind, scaffold-missing, contract-violated, or virgin) without writing.

args.name: project
args.help: Name of the workspace project to split and push as a standalone mirror repo

graph.name: graph
graph.help: Export the monorepo dependency graph in JSON, DOT (Graphviz), or indented text tree format. Supports filtering by a root package (transitive deps) or reverse package (transitive rdeps), with optional depth limiting. Use --output to write to a file instead of stdout.

flags.name: format
flags.help: Serialization format for the dependency graph: json, dot (Graphviz), or text

flags.name: output
flags.help: File path to write the graph output to instead of printing to stdout

flags.name: root
flags.help: Filter to show only transitive dependencies reachable from this package

flags.name: reverse
flags.help: Filter to show only transitive reverse dependencies of this package

flags.name: depth
flags.help: Maximum number of dependency hops to traverse from the root or reverse node

impact.name: impact
impact.help: Analyze the impact of changes to a package, file, or git diff range on the monorepo dependency graph. Shows direct and transitive dependents, test scope, and release candidates. Supports package names, file paths, and --since for git-based change detection.

flags.name: format
flags.help: Output serialization format for the impact report: json or text (default: text)

flags.name: depth
flags.help: Maximum number of dependency hops to traverse when computing transitive impact

flags.name: since
flags.help: Git ref to diff against HEAD (e.g. HEAD~3, v1.0.0)

extract.name: extract
extract.help: Extract a package from the monorepo into a new standalone repository. Clones the monorepo, runs git filter-repo to keep only the package's history, migrates changelog entries, creates .rlsbl/ config in the new repo, and removes the project from workspace.toml.

args.name: package_name
args.help: Name of the package as defined in workspace.toml to extract into a standalone repo

args.name: target_path
args.help: Filesystem path where the new standalone repository will be created

absorb.name: absorb
absorb.help: Absorb an external repository as a package in the monorepo. Rewrites the source's history to live under the destination path, fetch-merges it (preserving full history with rewritten paths), imports its version tags under the monorepo tag scheme, and remaps its JSONL changelog hashes to the new commits.

flags.name: name
flags.help: Workspace project name for the absorbed package (default: basename of the destination path)

flags.name: registry-name
flags.help: Package registry identity recorded in workspace.toml (used verbatim for name checks)

flags.name: releasable
flags.help: Releasable group to assign the absorbed package to

args.name: source_repo
args.help: Filesystem path to the external git repository to absorb

args.name: dest_path
args.help: Destination directory (and workspace path) the source repo's history is rewritten under

extract-releasable.name: extract-releasable
extract-releasable.help: Extract all member packages of a releasable into a new repository. If the releasable has one member, creates a single-project repo. If it has multiple members, creates a new monorepo with workspace.toml. Migrates changelog entries for each member and removes all extracted projects from the source workspace.

args.name: releasable_name
args.help: Name of the releasable group in workspace.toml to extract

args.name: target_path
args.help: Filesystem path where the new repository will be created

cleanup.name: cleanup
cleanup.help: Remove per-package release-state residue from releasable member packages: .rlsbl/changes/, .rlsbl/releases/, .rlsbl/bases/, .rlsbl/lint/, .rlsbl/version, per-package CHANGELOG.md, and .rlsbl/config.json when identical to the releasable-level config. Per-package hooks/ directories are preserved (live feature), and members whose path is the workspace root are exempt. Deletions go through saferm (audit trail, recoverable) and are committed automatically. Requires an explicit-mode workspace ([[releasables]] in workspace.toml). Detect residue first with `rlsbl check --name releasable-residue`.

migrate-releasable.name: migrate-releasable
migrate-releasable.help: Migrate a releasable from per-package release state to the releasable model. Detects current state, consolidates per-package changelogs and versions into the releasable directory, creates a releasable-format migration tag, and removes orphaned per-package .rlsbl/changes/ and .rlsbl/releases/ directories. Requires the workspace to be in explicit mode (with [[releasables]] in workspace.toml).

args.name: releasable_name
args.help: Name of the releasable group in workspace.toml to migrate

rename-releasable.name: rename-releasable
rename-releasable.help: Rename a releasable group. Rewrites the [[releasables]] name and every member's releasable field in workspace.toml (preserving comments), moves the releasable's state directory, drops the stale changelog validation cache, re-runs monorepo sync to regenerate publish gate prefixes, and commits everything as one commit. When the tag_format contains {name}, a boundary alias tag for the current version is created at the old tag's commit and pushed; historical releases stay under the old prefix. Idempotent: a crash between the commit and the tag push is healed by re-running.

args.name: old_name
args.help: Current name of the releasable group in workspace.toml

args.name: new_name
args.help: New name for the releasable group in workspace.toml and state directories

release.name: release
release.help: Release commands for monorepo workspaces. Provides 3 subcommands: run (batch release), init (scaffold release file), and order (topological release order).

run.name: run
run.help: Execute a batch release of multiple monorepo packages in topological order. Reads package configurations from .rlsbl-monorepo/releases/unreleased.toml. Each package is released sequentially using the single-package release flow, with leaves (no dependencies) released first. Supports --dry-run, --yes, --allow-dirty flags.

flags.name: push-timeout
flags.help: Timeout in seconds for each git push. Overrides the push_timeout config key; 0 (the default) means use push_timeout, else the shipped default.

flags.name: ci-timeout
flags.help: Timeout in seconds for the release CI gate (the wait for CI to conclude on the pushed release candidate). Overrides the ci_timeout config key; 0 (the default) means use ci_timeout, else the shipped default.

flags.name: check-timeout
flags.help: Timeout in seconds for each preflight check subprocess (tests, lint, external checks). Overrides the check_timeout config key; 0 (the default) means use check_timeout, else the shipped default.

flags.name: hook-timeout
flags.help: Timeout in seconds for each release hook. Overrides the hook_timeout config key; 0 (the default) means use hook_timeout, else no timeout.

flags.name: watch
flags.help: After batch release, automatically watch CI runs to completion (--no-watch to skip)

flags.name: allow-dirty
flags.help: Skip the clean working tree check and allow releasing with uncommitted changes

init.name: init
init.help: Scaffold a batch release file for all workspace projects by auto-detecting each project's release targets and generating per-package configuration sections. Creates .rlsbl-monorepo/releases/unreleased.toml with a [packages.<name>] section for each non-dev-node project, pre-populated with bump type, description, and include lists. Packages with no unreleased commits since their last tag are rendered as commented-out sections.

flags.name: packages
flags.help: Comma-separated package names to include (default: all)

order.name: order
order.help: Compute and display the topological release order for all projects in the monorepo workspace based on their declared depends-on relationships. Projects with no dependencies are listed first, followed by projects that depend on them, ensuring each project is released only after its dependencies. Detects and reports circular dependency errors.

dev.name: dev
dev.help: Developer utilities for locally working with rlsbl projects, including editable installs that mirror the project's release target (pypi -> uv tool install -e, npm -> npm link, go -> go install).

install.name: install
install.help: Install the project locally for development by running each detected target's own install command. --global (default) is supported by 7 targets: pypi (uv tool install -e), npm (npm link), go (go install), deno (deno install), and -- since they have no system-wide install concept -- zig (zig build install), swift (swift build), and hex (mix deps.get). --venv installs into the project's local environment instead and is supported by pypi, npm, deno, and hex; other targets are skipped with a reason. --uninstall reverses a previous install where the target supports it (pypi, npm, deno). In monorepo mode, pair with --all, --include, or --exclude.

flags.name: all
flags.help: In monorepo mode, install every project in the workspace

flags.name: include
flags.help: In monorepo mode, comma-separated project names to include

flags.name: exclude
flags.help: In monorepo mode, comma-separated project names to exclude

flags.name: uninstall
flags.help: Reverse a previous dev install (where supported by the target)

flags.name: global
flags.help: Install as a global tool/symlink. This is the default behavior when neither --global nor --venv is passed. Mutually exclusive with --venv.

flags.name: venv
flags.help: Install into the project's local environment only (e.g. uv sync, npm install). Mutually exclusive with --global.

sync.name: sync
sync.help: Overlay local editable checkouts of sibling projects onto this project's locked environment. Reads dev-sources.toml.local-only for overlay entries, runs uv sync --inexact excluding overlaid packages, then uv pip install -e per entry. Requires UV_NO_SYNC=1 in the environment to prevent bare uv run from reverting overlays.

status.name: status
status.help: Report the state of local dev-sync overlays: for each package recorded in the dev-overlays sentinel, show its declared editable checkout path and version alongside the venv's actual install (editable at the expected path, WIPED back to a registry wheel, or missing entirely). Exits 1 if any overlay drifted so scripts and pre-run guards can detect a silent wipe by a bare uv sync or uv run; exits 0 when all overlays are intact or none are declared.

handshakes.help: Pre-push ref lines (`<local ref> <local sha> <remote ref> <remote sha>`) for `rlsbl check --tag prepush`, when the caller has already consumed git's hook stdin.
